title: How many dosas does the rice price buy?
description: A dosa price in paise is written in rupees, and the price of a kilogram of rice is compared with it in paise. Keeko's doubt is that the rice price buys five dosas.
teaching_notes: One idea: write both prices in the same unit before dividing. Watch for students who round four point nine up to five dosas.

source: A masala dosa cost 50 paise in the 1970s, and a kg of rice cost ₹2.45. Write the dosa price in rupees, and say how many such dosas the rice price would buy.
video_script.why: The child has changed paise into rupees and now uses it to compare two prices.
video_script.substitution: Write both prices in the same unit, paise, then divide to count how many dosas the rice price buys.
video_script.anchor: a dosa priced at fifty paise beside a kilogram of rice priced at two rupees forty-five paise
video_script.wrong_move: rounds four point nine up to five and buys a part of a dosa
video_script.payoff_line: Write both prices in paise, then divide

final_answer.value: ₹0.50 for the dosa; ₹2.45 buys 4 dosas with 45 paise left
final_answer.spoken: zero point five zero rupees for the dosa; the rice price buys four dosas with forty-five paise left

hold_back: ₹0.50 for the dosa; ₹2.45 buys 4 dosas with 45 paise left
maths_rules: check: 4 x 50 = 200 paise and 245 - 200 = 45 paise left
the slip: 5 dosas would cost 250 paise, which is more than 245 paise
video_script.design: The dosa and the rice stay in the anchor band with their prices. Both prices slide into the working band in paise, the division is shown, and a check multiplies four dosas back.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book, then a masala dosa marked 50 paise and a kilogram of rice marked ₹2.45; a question mark in the anchor band

marks.list: the dosa and the rice are drawn with their prices

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about prices long ago.
<bookmark mark='list'/>A masala dosa cost fifty paise. A kilogram of rice cost two rupees forty-five paise.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We write the dosa price in rupees and count how many dosas the rice price buys.

beats.on_screen: the prices stay on the board; Keeko sits beside them as the child
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 1 rupee = 100 paise shown as a coin; two prices in different units written side by side

marks.coin: the coin is shown with 100 paise
marks.same: the two prices are placed in the same unit

narration: <bookmark mark='coin'/>A rupee has one hundred paise, so we can change between the two.
<bookmark mark='same'/>To compare two prices, we write them in the same unit.

beats.on_screen: Given: a dosa at 50 paise and a kilogram of rice at ₹2.45
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a dosa at fifty paise and a kilogram of rice at two point four five rupees.

beats.on_screen: To find: the dosa price in rupees, and the number of dosas the rice price buys
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write the dosa price in rupees and count the dosas the rice price buys.
<bookmark mark='p50'/>Step one, fifty paise is fifty hundredths of a rupee.
<bookmark mark='dec'/>That is zero point five zero rupees.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: ₹2.45 x 100 = 245 paise; the point moves 2 places right

marks.back: an arrow shows rupees going to paise

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step two, write the rice price in paise.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>We multiply by one hundred, so the point moves two places right.
<bookmark mark='p245'/>Two point four five rupees is two hundred forty-five paise.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Step three, divide two hundred forty-five by fifty.
<bookmark mark='quo'/>That gives four point nine.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>Four whole dosas are bought, and a little money is left.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check 4 x 50 = 200 paise; 245 - 200 = 45 paise left
narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step four, four dosas cost two hundred paise.
<bookmark mark='left'/>The rice price is two hundred forty-five, so forty-five paise are left.

beats.on_screen: Answer: ₹0.50 for the dosa; ₹2.45 buys 4 dosas with 45 paise left

marks.rice: the four dosas and the leftover are marked

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Write both prices in paise, then divide.
<bookmark mark='dosa'/>A dosa costs zero point five zero rupees.
<bookmark mark='rice'/>The rice price buys four dosas, with forty-five paise left.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the dosa
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 5 dosas appears and is struck out; 5 x 50 = 250 paise is written beside 245 paise; 4 dosas is written

marks.fix: 5 x 50 = 250 paise is written beside 245 paise
marks.four: 5 dosas is struck out and 4 dosas is written

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the rice price buys five dosas, because four point nine is almost five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But five dosas cost two hundred fifty paise, and the rice price is only two hundred forty-five.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four point nine means four whole dosas and a part of the fifth. We cannot buy a part, so it is four dosas.
